newsitem.title: USA: FIGURE SKATING-ELDREDGE LEADS AFTER SHORT PROGRAM.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-ELDREDGE LEADS AFTER SHORT PROGRAM.

text.p: World champion Todd Eldredge of the United States took the lead in the men's competition after the short programme at Skate America International on Thursday.
"Nothing special," Eldredge said of his performance, which gave him the lead over Russia's Alexei Urmanov entering tomorrow's free-skating programme.
"Training has been going well for the past few weeks, and I think that gives you confidence."
Eldredge's coach, Richard Callaghan, said he was pleased but "some of the elements we'll want a little better as we go into later competitions."
Takeshi Honda of Japan was third after the short programme.

The competition, the first major international event of the figure-skating season, is one of six events in the Champions Series. Winners receive prize money and points toward qualifying for the Champion Final Series February, 28-March, 2 in Hamilton, Canada. This weekend's competition is the only event in the series staged in the United States.
Americans Shelby Lyons and Brian Wells took a surprising lead in the pairs competition after last night's short programme.
The Russian team of former Olympic gold and silver medalist Artur Dmitriev and his partner since 1995, Oksana Kazakova, was second.
In the dance competition, Russian skaters Anjelika Krylova and Oleg Ovsiannikov led after the compulsories, followed by another Russian team, Irina Lobatcheva and Ilia Averbukh.
In pairs, coach Irina Vorobieva said she felt her team of Lyons and Wells was on the verge of establishing a greater presence on the world stage.
"They've had some good results at lower level, and I think they're ready for good results here," she said. "I feel more comfortable - it's a good start, but it's not finished."
